parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal document/entry layer with an actively enforced state facility law. Foreign posts refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding; multiple governments now advise trans citizens against travel. In-state, restroom access is keyed to birth-certificate sex across schools, universities and state buildings, enforced within days via ID checks, with trespass exposure and a documented analogue arrest held in a men's ward. Immigration custody carries documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse of trans detainees. Offsetting this: no criminalisation of identity as such, several orders enjoined, trans women with matching markers admitted at checks, and a national hate-crime statute. Violence counts lack denominators. Overall tier-1/tier-2 exposures with partial, contested remedies place this in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order defines binary sex at conception/birth; X markers and non-assigned-sex markers halted for new issues; consular cable orders refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, with consideration of a permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility finding; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated and stranded abroad; eight-plus governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; the policy is under active litigation by a civil-liberties union; a legal-aid FAQ advises on documentation and name/marker interaction.
entry_documents.interaction: State definition act bans marker changes on licences/birth certificates and ties facility access to birth-certificate sex, compounding federal entry screening for a visitor whose documents are inspected at a state building or checkpoint.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans people in immigration custody reportedly subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; a trans woman arrested under an analogue bathroom law was held 24 hours in a men's ward; state prison denial of gender-confirmation surgery upheld by an appeals court; national corrections bureau adopting conversion-therapy-style policies.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Facility offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; ID checks at the capitol admitted trans women holding female markers; several federal orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate into fraud investigation, immigration detention and then birth-sex-congruent placement, chaining federal screening to custody harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State women's-privacy statute (effective 4 Dec 2025) requires restrooms matching birth-certificate sex in public schools, universities, prisons and state buildings, with $25k/$125k facility fines; enforcement began within days via trooper ID checks; federally, an executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; four states criminalise access in certain circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Reach is largely government-owned settings; private venues mostly unaffected in this state; only two enforcement episodes documented; unclear guidance produces uneven rather than systematic sweeps.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor entering a capitol, university or state office moves from private space into a birth-sex rule enforced by officers checking identification.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care banned for minors since June 2023 following a 2022 child-abuse opinion; subpoenaed youth medical records; LGBTQ youth lifeline services shut; proposed national insurance bar for under-18s; adult access restriction bills filed but status not sourced.
care_services.protection: Directives on parent investigation partially enjoined and several DAs refused to enforce; several federal orders blocked or enjoined in court.
care_services.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor may face care denial and, if directives revive, state inquiry into facilitating transition — resident machinery reaching a visiting family.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; January 2025 order directs law enforcement to investigate schools and prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; binary-sex definition act; governor directive recognising only two genders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo does not list gender ideology as a reward criterion; the strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; advocates' genocide-stage comparison remains advocacy framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing licenses state enforcement posture, e.g. DOJ's escalated complaint against a school district under the state bathroom law.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors denied gender-affirming care since 2023; parental-rights statute mandates deadnaming/misgendering and bans LGBT student groups; mandatory investigation directives with criminal failure-to-report penalties (partly enjoined); EO threatens prosecution of teachers; a guardian travelling with a trans minor could encounter care denial and state inquiry.
minors_guardians.protection: Temporary injunction blocking parent-investigation directives, reinstated on appeal; five DAs refused the directives; injunctions on several federal orders.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting family moves between a federal order framing minor care as abuse and state family-services powers, with courts partially but not fully restraining both.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute covers sexual orientation but not gender identity and prosecutions are rare; no statewide discrimination ban in employment, housing or public accommodations; police ID checks at restrooms; LGB visibility rolling back (ordinance rescinded, Pride suspended); public opinion backs birth-sex document rules (66%).
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several cities bar gender-identity discrimination; state courts recognised the national employment ruling.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin state-level recourse means a visitor assaulted in a locality without city ordinances relies on federal statutes and reluctant local police.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: July 2026 legal-risk assessment places the state in the top 'Do Not Travel' tier for adult trans travellers; unclear facility guidance; school-district investigation outcome unsourced; no later enforcement episode documented; unresolved litigation makes exposure time-dependent; violence counts lack denominators so magnitude is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple successful injunctions; running legal-aid FAQ; national employment and hate-crime protections; foreign advisories give advance warning; documented case of matching-marker ID checks admitting trans women.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Contested federal litigation means remedies exist but outcomes at a given moment of travel are uncertain, so paper recourse only partly offsets operative rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Saruth combines routine border detention in crowded cells, tolerated assaults, withheld care, delayed habeas and residual capital language. Here entry refusal is conditional (document discrepancy or doubt), functioning courts have enjoined multiple orders, and no capital or torture pathway for visitors is documented — though immigration-custody abuse is a serious shared feature. Materially higher than 0.15.

Vellandra bars entry to any trans visitor deemed noncompliant, routinely and discretionarily, with appeals to the same agency. This dossier's consular cable also produces exclusion without charge, but only on documented discrepancy/doubt, with pending litigation, valid existing X passports and no registration regime. Close to this anchor, marginally above it.

Kestrel Isles shows extended secondary screening, humiliating delays and slow, rarely revised refusal appeals — entry friction comparable to this dossier's border layer. But this jurisdiction adds an actively enforced state birth-sex facility law with ID checks and trespass exposure, custody-abuse documentation and no statewide discrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage. Lower than 0.55.

Meridia-trained border staff, tribunal review, written reasons and compensation for unlawful holding assume recognising, remedy-delivering institutions. Here officers are instructed toward refusal, state recourse excludes gender identity from hate-crime coverage, and a July 2026 assessment grades the state 'Do Not Travel'. Materially lower than 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: Federal and state layers compound rather than offset. A trans visitor's home documents govern entry, but the consular cable converts any mismatch or doubt into refusal plus possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and trans people in immigration custody document beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse — so the worst chain runs document discrepancy → detention → abuse. Inside the state, birth-certificate-sex restroom rules across state buildings were enforced within days by ID checks, backed by fines and a trespass offence, with an analogue arrest held in a men's ward; guidance remains unclear, so exposure is continuous though uneven. Recourse is partial: courts have enjoined several federal orders, matching-marker ID holders were admitted, and a national hate-crime statute covers gender identity — but the state lacks discrimination coverage, excludes gender identity from its hate-crime law, bans minor care, and is graded top 'Do Not Travel'.
